Port of Palm Beach The Port of Palm Beach is 80 miles north of Miami and 135 miles south of Port Canaveral. The Port and its tenants combine to be one of the larger employers in Palm Beach County and is an economic engine for the county. The Port of Palm Beach is the fourth busiest container port of Florida’s 14 deepwater ports and is the 18th busiest container port in the United States, with ample resources for MTV outfitting and other needs. Port Everglades Port Everglades in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, is conveniently situated near the Atlantic Ocean shipping lanes, the Florida East Coast Railway, Florida's highway system, and the Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. In 2019, Port Everglades was ranked the third-busiest cruise homeport in the world, accommodating more than 3.89 million passengers. It is also one of the busiest container ports in Florida and ranked among the top 20 busiest in the United States, moving more than 1 million TEUs annually. Port Everglades is the #1 seaport in Florida by revenue and one of the top container ports in the state. FAU also operates an ocean engineering research campus 3 mi. south of the port with a minimum of 30 m of Intracoastal Waterway seawall and dockage access. 14.4 Estimated Cost of Ownership The MTV’s cost of ownership is the aggregate of costs associated with MTV Modes of Operation 5-8. These Modes of Operation represent all modes where the MTV is not in service. Costs can be viewed in the following categories: personnel, equipment, materials and supplies, travel, and vendor services (including equipment service contracts). Where actual costs are not known, historical or analog experiences were used to provide a range of costs for scale. The MTV’s onboard systems are not nearly as complex as a ship’s because they do not include propulsion, habitation, or other related capabilities. It is also expected that full-time crew and maintenance personnel will not be required when not in-service, the MTV has no engines that need regular overhaul, and supplies requirements will be significantly less (no major provisioning). The MTV will only require minor direct administrative support to assist with scheduling and managing cost center accounting. Administrative support for procurement and personnel is not expected to be directly costed to the operation of the MTV. In this way, the cost of ownership of the MTV can be minimized and managed to reduce costs to both FAU and MTV users. Anticipated costs were developed for each operational mode associated with the cost of ownership, and a rough-order-of-magnitude annual estimate was developed. With respect to analogous annual historical R/V Seward Johnson costs, MTV cost of ownership is similarly allocated. When R/V Seward Johnson engine overhaul and crew costs are excluded, administration costs represent 33% of total costs, maintenance 41%, and supplies 26%.
